entities.summary: Lexicography is the study of lexicons and the art of compiling dictionaries. It is divided into two separate academic disciplines:Practical lexicography is the compiling, writing, and editing of dictionaries. Theoretical lexicography is the scholarly study of semantic, orthographic, syntagmatic, and paradigmatic features of lexemes of the lexicon (vocabulary) of a language, developing theories of dictionary components and structures linking the data in dictionaries, the needs for information by users in specific types of situations, and how users may best access the data incorporated in printed and electronic dictionaries.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Lexicography played a crucial role in the development of modern languages, with the first comprehensive dictionaries emerging during the Renaissance. The invention of the printing press allowed for mass production of dictionaries, making language learning and documentation more accessible.
